Competencies

Show indicators at

Showing the L3 indicator for each competency. Open a competency to see all five levels.

  • Sources identification4.5.1

    L1 Awareness

    Recognise the main mineable pharma sources (EHR, claims, registries, literature, social media, sensor streams).

    L2 Familiarity

    Describe a single pharma source: structure, biases, access route.

    L3 Proficiency

    Identify and qualify the right mining sources for a real pharma question.

    L4 Mastery

    Combine multiple sources into a defensible mining design with awareness of biases and gaps.

    L5 Expertise

    Set the team's source-identification practice.

  • Pattern/association rule mining4.5.2

    L1 Awareness

    Recognise association rules and itemset / co-occurrence mining.

    L2 Familiarity

    Run a small arules/mlxtend analysis on a pharma sample following an example.

    L3 Proficiency

    Apply association mining to a real pharma question (co-prescribing, AE co-occurrence) with appropriate filters and interpretation.

    L4 Mastery

    Handle non-trivial mining (rare events, hierarchical items, statistical correction) on real pharma data.

    L5 Expertise

    Does not apply at this level. further mastery folds into broader Mining or Modelling competencies

  • Text mining (NLP) & information extraction4.5.3

    L1 Awareness

    Recognise NLP tasks relevant to pharma: classification, NER, normalisation to ontologies.

    L2 Familiarity

    Run a basic NLP pipeline (tokenisation, NER) on pharma text following an example.

    L3 Proficiency

    Apply NLP to a real pharma question (extracting outcomes, adverse events, eligibility from clinical text) with evaluation.

    L4 Mastery

    Handle hard pharma NLP — domain adaptation, noisy text, multilingual data, weak supervision, LLM-assisted extraction with validation.

    L5 Expertise

    Lead pharma NLP practice or contribute methods.

  • Graph/network-based mining4.5.4

    L1 Awareness

    Recognise graphs / networks (drug–target, co-prescription, citation) as a mining substrate.

    L2 Familiarity

    Build and visualise a small pharma graph following an example.

    L3 Proficiency

    Run graph algorithms (centrality, community detection) on real pharma networks and interpret results.

    L4 Mastery

    Apply advanced graph methods (graph ML, link prediction) to real pharma problems with careful evaluation.

    L5 Expertise

    Lead graph-analytics practice in the team.

  • Time-series & process mining4.5.5

    L1 Awareness

    Recognise time-series forecasting and process mining as distinct disciplines.

    L2 Familiarity

    Fit a basic time-series model or run a simple process-mining tool on pharma data following an example.

    L3 Proficiency

    Apply time-series or process mining to a real pharma question (treatment pathways, adverse-event trends, sensor signals).

    L4 Mastery

    Handle hard cases — irregular sampling, regime change, multiple time scales, complex pathways — defensibly.

    L5 Expertise

    Set the team's standards for temporal and process analytics.

Pharma examples

Each example is tagged with the competency and level it shows. Tags open that level.

  • Mining adverse-event term co-occurrence in spontaneous reportsPattern/association rule mining L3
  • Information extraction from oncology pathology reportsText mining (NLP) & information extraction L4
  • Treatment-pathway analysis from claims using process miningTime-series & process mining L4

Typical stack

classic mining (arules, mlxtend); NLP (spaCy, udpipe, tidytext, transformers); graph analytics (igraph, networkx, tidygraph); time-series and process mining (prophet, tsfeatures, pm4py).
